items.headline: Dollar stretches to a fresh 19-month high in Asia — DXY 103.66, a seventh straight up day; EUR/USD below 1.1000 (low 1.0985), GBP/USD ~$1.3179, USD/JPY ~159.49, still capped below 160. Dec Fed 25bp hike ~90-93%, 50bp tail ~7-8%.

RBA minutes: six of nine judged 4.85% 'not clearly sufficient' to tame inflation; three warned of a sharper downturn. AUD ~$0.6740, little changed; ANZ/CBA/Goldman call 4.85% the peak. Next decision Dec 8.
RBA Gov Bullock (ASIC forum): inflation risks 'skewed to the upside'; the hikes were 'not just a response to oil prices' — the RBA started tightening before the Middle East conflict lifted crude.

RBNZ Financial Stability Report: global financial-stability risks keep rising, but the NZ system can withstand shocks; domestic stress eased from last year's peak but stays uneven (Breman). NZD/USD ~$0.5497.

CFTC Nov 10 COT (released Mon): EUR net short -136,396 (3rd pct, stretched short, 6th week); JPY net long +123,113 (90th pct); AUD net short -151,753 (1st pct, record gross shorts); CHF shorts unwinding (94th pct); GBP -43,216, CAD -32,592, NZD -55,366; DXY futures +13,813.
Gold hits a one-year low — spot ~$3,855 (-0.8%) as the firmer dollar and ~90% odds of a Dec Fed hike cap the metal; overnight low ~$3,832, capped by the 50-hour average ~$3,878.
Oil slide extends overnight — Brent ~$91.65, WTI ~$84.90, ~0.9% below Monday's settles, as the IEA's Q4 surplus call (1.7 mb/d) and nearly restored Hormuz flows keep the surplus trade going.
Tech rout deepens Monday — Nasdaq -2.5%, Dow -739 points as the Nvidia leadership crisis and Anthropic's record IPO jitters hit the AI trade; S&P -1.0%. Nvidia reports after the close today.

Today: UK earnings 1:00am CT (3.5% fcst); US retail sales 7:30am CT (+0.1% m/m fcst, control +0.4%); Nvidia earnings after the close; AU wage price index 6:30pm CT (1.0% fcst). Wed: UK CPI 1:00am CT (3.6%), FOMC minutes 1:00pm CT; Thu: AU jobs 6:30pm CT, Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen.

Dollar holds a fresh 19-month high into the New York close — DXY ~103.59 (6th straight up); EUR/USD ~$1.1003, a 19-month low; GBP/USD ~$1.3189; USD/JPY ~159.55, capped below 160 by intervention watch; AUD/USD ~$0.6754; NZD/USD ~$0.5515. Dec Fed 25bp hike ~93-94%, 50bp tail ~6%.

Oil slides — Brent ~$92.29 (-2.7%), WTI ~$85.45 (-2.6%) as the IEA's Q4 surplus call (1.7 mb/d) lands with Hormuz flows nearly restored; Goldman sees Brent averaging $88 in 2027 and $78 by year-end as supply outstrips demand by ~2 mb/d.

Fed Chair Warsh gives opening remarks at the Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference (San Francisco) — Fed staff modeling three AI scenarios (productivity gains, job losses, stock slump); no rate proposal, no December steer. Dec 25bp hike ~93-94% stands; FOMC minutes Wed 1:00pm CT.

BoC Dec hike odds trimmed to ~44% after October CPI (Morningstar/Dow Jones, from ~60% pre-print; Polymarket 44.5% hike / 55% hold) — CPI +3.1% y/y vs 3.2% consensus, core anchored near 2%; hold stays the base case, January more likely. USD/CAD ~1.4297 into the close.

Empire State Manufacturing MISSES — +7.8 in November vs +16.7 expected (Oct 25.5, a multiyear high); new orders nearly stall at 3.0 (from 23.2), shipments 8.8; hiring jumps to 18.1, its highest since June 2022; prices paid ease to 45.9. A mixed soft read; Dec Fed hike pricing unmoved.

Canada CPI +3.1% y/y in October (vs 3.2% consensus; Sep 3.1%), +0.2% m/m (vs 0.3%); ex food & energy +1.8% y/y (vs 1.9%); BoC core median 2.0%, trim 1.8%, common 2.5% — core anchored near 2%, so the Dec 9 BoC hike case does not strengthen; hold stays the base case, January more likely (ING). USD/CAD ~1.4291 pre-print, probing the 1.4299 Oct top.

Eurozone industrial production MISSES — +0.2% m/m in September vs +0.3% expected (Aug -0.5%); -1.5% y/y vs -0.2% expected. First rise in four months, but ING: 'no signs of a true rebound', only modest gains ahead.

Japan Q3 GDP contracts 0.1% annualized vs +0.3% expected — first contraction in a year; q/q 0.0% vs +0.1% fcst; consumption -0.3%, capex +1.6% beat, net exports -0.6pp drag. USD/JPY flat ~159.6-159.7 — the miss has not moved the yen or the Dec BoJ hike case (~84% intact); Katayama intervention warning still the cap near 160.

Reuters poll: most economists expect the ECB to deliver a final deposit-rate hike in December, more than a third expect another in early 2027 as inflation runs at double the 2% target; Dec hike ~88-92% priced. EUR/USD ~$1.1025 in Asia.
